actions.TEMPORARY_IP_BLOCK_desc: Activate NetworkPolicy or WAF rules to block anomalous source IP ranges causing traffic overload.
actions.RESTART_DEPLOYMENT_desc: Trigger rollout restart for the entire Deployment to refresh service instance state.

actions.SCALE_REPLICAS_desc: Automatically increase Pod Replicas to distribute load and restore service capacity per MAPE‑K.
actions.ROLLBACK_DEPLOYMENT_desc: Revert to the previous stable ReplicaSet to eliminate CrashLoop errors after a new release.
actions.SCALE_DOWN_desc: Automatically reduce Pod Replicas during sustained low load to optimize infrastructure cost per MAPE-K.

inspector.ruleR1Title: Rule R1: High CPU with Slow Latency
inspector.ruleR1Summary: Jointly checks both CPU and latency of "{{service}}". Triggers only when BOTH exceed thresholds (CPU > 80% AND Latency > 200ms) to prevent false alarms when CPU spikes briefly while response remains fast.
inspector.ruleR1Next: When both conditions exceed thresholds → Routes directly to Multi-Agent RCA (prioritizing Scale Replicas or Restart Pod).
inspector.ruleR2Title: Rule R2: Traffic Surge with Low Replicas
inspector.ruleR2Summary: Detects incoming traffic surge to "{{service}}" (> 500 req/s) while running replicas are thin (≤ 2 Pods), risking bottlenecks or cascading outages.
inspector.ruleR2Next: When triggered → Multi-Agent RCA inspects whether it is a DDoS flood or legitimate load to recommend Scale Replicas or Temporary IP Block.
inspector.ruleR3SummaryDb: Service "{{service}}" uses page buffer caching (WiredTiger Cache). High steady RAM is normal I/O optimization for databases, with no OOM risk as there are no OOMKilled events or Pod restarts.
inspector.ruleR3Summary: Monitors RAM of "{{service}}". If RAM exceeds 85% or Kubernetes logs an OOMKilled event (container killed for memory overflow), the rule immediately triggers at 95% confidence.
inspector.ruleR3NextDb: Autonomous safeguard stays active, avoiding unintended Pod restarts on database workloads.
inspector.ruleR3Next: When triggered → Routes to Multi-Agent RCA to diagnose Memory Leak and recommend Restart / Replace Pod.
inspector.ruleR4Title: Rule R4: HTTP 5xx Server Error Spike
inspector.ruleR4Summary: Watches server error responses (500, 502, 503, 504) on "{{service}}". Once error rate exceeds 5%, end users are directly impacted and incident handling starts immediately.
inspector.ruleR4Next: When triggered → Multi-Agent RCA scans error Container Logs to pick Restart Pod, Rollback (via HITL), or Circuit Breaker.
inspector.ruleR5Summary: Directly monitors container health of "{{service}}" on the Kubernetes cluster. Triggers on abnormal restarts (Restart ≥ 1), CrashLoopBackOff, or Health Probe failures (Unhealthy).
inspector.ruleR5Next: When triggered → Multi-Agent RCA inspects K8s Events & Logs to find crash root cause before Replace Pod or Rollback.
inspector.ruleR6Summary: Early warning when disk usage of "{{service}}" exceeds 85% (often caused by growing logs or temp files), preventing total application hangs.
inspector.ruleR6Next: When triggered → Multi-Agent RCA verifies storage capacity and recommends Cleanup Temp Files.

metricDesc.cpu: Measures CPU utilization (%) of service containers over the last 60-second window.
metricDesc.ram: Measures RAM utilization (%). Steadily rising RAM without release indicates a Memory Leak risking OOMKilled.
metricDesc.disk: Measures disk space percentage consumed by the app, logs, or temporary files.
metricDesc.latency: Measures response latency (ms). Spikes indicate resource contention, DB overload, or internal network issues.
metricDesc.request_rate: Measures incoming requests per second (Req/s) to detect traffic surges or idle load.
metricDesc.http_5xx_rate: Measures percentage of requests returning HTTP 5xx server errors (500–504).
metricDesc.pod_restart_count: Measures container restart counts within the monitoring window to detect recurring CrashLoopBackOff or OOMKilled.
metricDesc.replica_count: Measures available Pod replicas ready to serve traffic on Kubernetes.
metricDesc.default: Telemetry metric collected directly from Kubernetes cluster every 5 seconds.

inspector.metricNext: Data is routed simultaneously to 2 branches: Rule Engine (instant threshold check) and AI (12-step sequence forecast).
inspector.riskSummary: AI model probability forecast across the 12-step sequence (60s) for "{{service}}". If probability exceeds this head's threshold, AI automatically triggers Root Cause Analysis (RCA).
inspector.riskNextTriggered: Threshold exceeded → Red signal pushed to Multi-Agent RCA for root cause diagnosis.
inspector.riskNextSafe: Below safety threshold → System continues monitoring next 12-step cycle.
inspector.gruSummary: Accumulates a fresh 12-step telemetry batch (Tumbling Batch: 12 × 5s = 60s) and feeds the [12×8] matrix into the AI model to forecast 7 risks before incidents occur.
inspector.gruNext: The 7-head forecast results are pushed over WebSocket to Dashboard and trigger Multi-Agent RCA if thresholds are breached.
inspector.rcaSummary: When AI or Rule Engine flags an anomaly, 4 specialized agents (Metrics, Log, K8s Event, History) gather evidence for "{{service}}", then RootCauseAgent determines root cause and RecommendationAgent proposes remediation.
inspector.rcaNextOpen: Remediation proposal is forwarded to Policy Engine (Stage 05) to verify autonomous execution permissions vs. human approval.
inspector.rcaNextIdle: No open incidents on this service — RCA is on standby.
inspector.policySummary: Evaluates AI recommendations against organization self-healing policies: enforces anti-spam Cooldown, minimum AI Confidence, and mandatory HITL gates for high-risk actions (ROLLBACK, DRAIN_NODE, primary DB).
inspector.policyNext: Automatically routes flow into 1 of 3 gates: AUTO execution, HITL approval, or Circuit Breaker.
inspector.autoSummary: Autonomously executes safe actions (Scale Replicas, Restart Pod, Cleanup Temp Files) by dispatching commands directly via WebSocket to the Self-Heal Agent on the Kubernetes cluster.
inspector.autoNext: Once K8s Agent completes the command, the system transitions to 60s Verification to confirm service stability.
inspector.hitlSummary: Human-in-the-Loop safety barrier: holds high-risk or low-confidence actions for "{{service}}" and notifies operators by email before modifying the Kubernetes cluster.
inspector.hitlNext: Once approved by an engineer → Command dispatches immediately to K8s Agent and enters 60s Verification.
inspector.auditSummary: When AI returns NO_ACTION (preventing endless remediation loops) or policy is in Audit/Disabled mode, the system makes NO K8s changes and records Audit Logs plus engineer alerts.
inspector.auditNext: Engineers inspect Audit Logs & Incidents for deeper code or infrastructure resolution.
inspector.verifySummary: Verifies outcome after each Action (e.g., Action #1: Restart Pod). After Stage 06 executes on "{{service}}", the system waits for a fresh 12-step batch (60s): if Recovered → auto-resolves incident (RESOLVED); if Unrecovered → loops back to RCA to escalate to Action #2 or trip Circuit Breaker.
inspector.verifyTotalAll: Total {{total}} tried in 24h: {{succeeded}} recovered • {{failed}} unrecovered on service:
inspector.verifyNextZeroPods: Service currently has 0 Pods on cluster. Once deployed/restarted, telemetry collection and monitoring resume at Stage 01.
inspector.verifyNextUnrecovered: Previous action did not fully recover → Feedback returns to Stage 01 & Multi-Agent RCA to escalate next action (or trip Circuit Breaker NO_ACTION).
inspector.verifyNextLoop: Closed loop complete: fresh telemetry streams back to Stage 01 for 24/7 continuous monitoring.

closedLoop.overviewSummary: Closed-Loop Autonomous Architecture designed following IBM's MAPE-K (Monitor - Analyze - Plan - Execute - Knowledge) standard for distributed Kubernetes systems. The platform continuously collects 60s telemetry, diagnoses root causes via Multi-Agent RCA, validates safety through the Policy Engine, executes remediation, and runs a 60s verification check to auto-resolve incidents or escalate actions.
closedLoop.overviewRowGuardVal: Policy Engine, Cooldown {{cooldown}}s, HITL Gate, Circuit Breaker
closedLoop.overviewNext: Click any phase block (Phase 01 to 04) in the loop diagram below to inspect operational details.
closedLoop.monitorSummary: Acts as the sensory layer of the autonomous system. Continuously collects 8 standard telemetry metrics (CPU, RAM, Disk, Latency, Request Rate, Error 5xx, Restarts, Replicas) from Prometheus and cAdvisor per Pod/Service every 5 seconds, aggregating a 12-step Sliding Window (60s). The [12×8] matrix is normalized and fed simultaneously to AI Hub and Rule Engine.
closedLoop.monitorRowDimsVal: 8 metrics (CPU, RAM, Disk, Latency, Req/s, 5xx, Restarts, Replicas)
closedLoop.monitorNext: The 12x8 telemetry matrix is passed to Phase 2 for GRU trend forecasting and Multi-Agent root-cause diagnosis.
closedLoop.analyzeSummary: Acts as the intelligent reasoning brain, combining two mechanisms: (1) Deep GRU model forecasting degradation risks over the next 60s (Proactive); (2) 4 Multi-Agent analysts (Metrics Agent, Log Agent, K8s Event Agent, History Agent) alongside Rule Engine R1→R6 cross-correlating faulty Pods, Root Cause, and AI confidence (55% - 95%).
closedLoop.analyzeRowModelVal: GRU Model (12 past steps → 12 future steps)
closedLoop.analyzeRowAgentsVal: 4 Agents: Metrics, Logs, K8s Events, History
closedLoop.analyzeNext: Once the root cause is identified, the remediation recommendation is handed off to Phase 3 (Policy Engine & K8s Action).
closedLoop.planSummary: Acts as the decision-maker and execution arm. Policy Engine performs safety checks (Cooldown {{cooldown}}s, Circuit Breaker retry limits, resource type protection), then routes to 3 branches: Autonomous AUTO (low-risk with high AI confidence), HITL Approval Gate (high-risk actions such as DaemonSet or destructive cleanup), or Circuit Breaker if retries are exhausted.
closedLoop.planRowActionsVal: Restart Pod, Replace Pod, Scale Replicas, Rollback
closedLoop.planRowDaemonVal: Auto CANCEL / REJECT when scaling down DaemonSets (e.g., kube-proxy)
closedLoop.planNext: Remediation command is sent to K8s API Server. Once completed, the system initiates Phase 4 (60s Verification).
closedLoop.verifySummary: Acts as post-remediation verification and closes the self-healing loop. After executing the K8s action, the system waits 60 seconds (one fresh 12-step telemetry batch) to re-evaluate live SLA metrics. If metrics return within safe bounds → Auto-Resolve incident and return to Phase 01. If issues persist after 60s → feed data back to Phase 02 (Multi-Agent RCA) to escalate the next action (or trip Circuit Breaker if retries exceed limit).
closedLoop.verifyRowSlaVal: Compares CPU, RAM, Latency, 5xx against safe thresholds
closedLoop.verifyRowSuccessVal: Auto-Resolve incident ➔ Return to Phase 01 for 24/7 monitoring
closedLoop.verifyRowFailVal: Feedback to Phase 02 ➔ Multi-Agent RCA escalates next Action
closedLoop.verifyNext: 100% autonomous closed-loop guaranteeing resilient self-healing without manual intervention.

memory_exhaustion.label: Container memory exhausted (OOM)
memory_exhaustion.reason: Tier-1 OOM prioritizes restarting Pod to free RAM; escalates to REPLACE_POD if recurring.

storage_exhaustion.label: Storage capacity exhausted
storage_exhaustion.reason: Disk > 85%, triggers safe automatic temp file & log cleanup (CLEANUP_STORAGE).

cpu_saturation.label: CPU resource saturation
cpu_saturation.reason: Two-Tier Capacity confirms Node headroom → auto-scales Replicas to distribute CPU load.

traffic_overload.label: Traffic overload
traffic_overload.reason: Sudden traffic spike → Auto Scale Replicas (or routes IP block via HITL if attack IP detected).

unstable_pod.label: Unstable application Pod / CrashLoop
unstable_pod.reason: Pod restarting repeatedly / CrashLoopBackOff → Provision fresh Pod (REPLACE_POD).

deployment_failure.label: New deployment release failure
deployment_failure.reason: New release causing errors → Proposes rollback to previous version via HITL Approval Gate.

dependency_failure.label: Upstream dependency failure
dependency_failure.reason: Upstream failure (external DB/API) → Enforces NO_ACTION guard to avoid pointless Pod restarts.

application_failure.label: Internal application error (HTTP 5xx)
application_failure.reason: Sporadic internal 5xx errors on Deployment → Rolling restart Deployment (or HITL Rollback if post-deploy).

service_degradation.label: Service performance degradation
service_degradation.reason: Latency exceeding SLO → Scale additional Replicas to share load (escalates to RESTART_POD if needed).

insufficient_replicas.label: Insufficient available Pod replicas
insufficient_replicas.reason: Available Pods below traffic demand → Auto-scales Replicas up to safe minimum.

scheduling_failure.label: Kubernetes scheduling failure
scheduling_failure.reason: Pods stuck Pending / Node overloaded → Proposes Drain Node to healthy Node (high risk → HITL approval).

underutilized.label: Underutilized resources (Scale down)
underutilized.reason: Sustained low load on multi-replica Deployment → Scales down Replicas to save capacity (blocked for DaemonSet).

probe_configuration_error.label: Health probe configuration error
probe_configuration_error.reason: Liveness/Readiness Probe timeout from YAML config → Cannot auto-edit YAML; alerts engineers via Audit.

network_degradation.label: Network connectivity degradation
network_degradation.reason: If flood/anomalous source IP detected → Temporary IP Block (HITL); if internal network fault → route to Audit.

database_cache_utilization.label: DB Buffer Cache (WiredTiger Cache)
database_cache_utilization.reason: Steady high RAM on DB without OOMKilled is normal Buffer Cache behavior → Protected by NO_ACTION, no DB restart.

unknown.label: Unknown (Insufficient evidence)
unknown.reason: Insufficient or conflicting evidence → Trips Circuit Breaker (NO_ACTION), writes Audit for human review.

RESTART_POD.label: Restart Pod
RESTART_POD.desc: Deletes current container process so kubelet restarts the Pod immediately.

SCALE_REPLICAS.label: Scale Pod Replicas
SCALE_REPLICAS.desc: Scales up or down replica count on Deployment/StatefulSet.

ROLLBACK_DEPLOYMENT.label: Rollback Deployment
ROLLBACK_DEPLOYMENT.desc: Reverts to the previous stable revision (requires HITL approval).

REPLACE_POD.label: Replace Pod
REPLACE_POD.desc: Fully removes failing Pod so Controller provisions a clean replacement Pod.

CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES.label: Cleanup Temp Storage
CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES.desc: Frees temporary files and bloated logs inside container (CLEANUP_STORAGE).

RESTART_DEPLOYMENT.label: Restart Deployment
RESTART_DEPLOYMENT.desc: Sequential zero-downtime rolling restart of all Deployment Pods.

ADJUST_RESOURCE_LIMITS.label: Adjust CPU/RAM Limits
ADJUST_RESOURCE_LIMITS.desc: Catalog CPU/RAM limit tuning (configured via Policy/Manual, not auto-triggered by AI).

DRAIN_NODE.label: Drain Node
DRAIN_NODE.desc: Cordons & drains all Pods from failing Node to healthy Node (requires HITL approval).

BLOCK_IP_TEMP.label: Temporary IP Block
BLOCK_IP_TEMP.desc: Applies NetworkPolicy to block flooding source IP temporarily (TEMPORARY_IP_BLOCK).

NO_ACTION.label: Safe Monitor / Circuit Break
NO_ACTION.desc: No K8s intervention; writes Audit Log & alerts when evidence is insufficient or DB cache is normal.
